    Linearizing inverse systems of sets (Lemma 4.1) #

    For an inverse system S of sets with surjective transition maps, the free vector spaces k^(S_i) form an inverse system with surjective transition maps. If moreover every countable set of indices is bounded and lim S = ∅, then lim k^(S_i) = 0 (Bergman [Be, Lemma 3], after Higman and Stone).

    Proof (finite supports): for a compatible family (v_i) with v_{i₀} ≠ 0, the support sizes |supp v_i| are monotone, hence eventually constant, because countable sets of indices are bounded. From then on, the transition maps restrict to bijections between supports, and lifting one point of a support through these bijections gives an element of lim S.
